title: When should a project stop expanding?
why_selected: Demonstrates the blind-first reading flow with synthetic content.
background: A small software project is technically feasible, but each additional feature adds maintenance cost. There is still little evidence that users need the larger scope.
question: Would you keep building, or pause and validate demand first? Which variables matter most?
author_reasoning: Technical feasibility and product value are separate questions. When demand is the largest uncertainty, the cheapest useful next step is to test actual usage before expanding engineering scope.
author_conclusion: Pause scope expansion, validate sustained use with the smallest credible test, and only then invest in a broader implementation.
